memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Your servant my father said to us, "You know that my wife bore me two sons. One of them went away from me, and I said, 'He has surely been torn to pieces.' And I have not seen him since. If you take this one from me too and harm comes to him, you will bring my grey head down to the grave in misery."'" — Gen 44:27-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Judah is quoting his father, and every word must have cut Joseph like a knife. "One of them went away from me... he has surely been torn to pieces." Those were the words Jacob spoke when the brothers showed him a bloodstained coat and let him believe a lie (Gen 37:33). Joseph is now hearing, for the first time, exactly what his disappearance did to his father.

And Judah is quoting it in front of the brothers who caused it. There is no hiding from what they did. The lie they told twenty years ago has been quietly grinding away at an old man's heart every single day since.

Sin is never contained. It never stays where we leave it. Every deception has a life of its own, and it goes on wounding people long after we have stopped thinking about it. The brothers moved on. Jacob never did.

If this makes you uncomfortable, let it. But do not stop there. The whole point of this chapter is that God is at work to heal exactly this kind of damage. What no amount of time could mend, God was arranging to restore. And He does it still — through the One who came to bind up the broken-hearted (Lk 4:18).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you considered how far the effects of your sin may have travelled?
2. Is there a relationship where a lie or silence is still doing damage?
3. Where do you need God's healing for something someone else's sin did to you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the harm my sin has caused others, some of which I may never fully see. Heal the wounds I have caused, and the wounds others have caused me. Thank You that Jesus binds up the broken-hearted. Amen.
